input: # Every other shared fixture asserts a decoded VALUE. That is one level too
# late for the defect class this project keeps hitting: BOTH upstream bug
# reports were token-classification splits — a run lexing #TX in one port
# and #NR in the other — and the wrong value was only the symptom. A
# value-only corpus catches those late, or not at all when two ports happen
# to coerce different tokens to the same value. Downstream treats its token
# stream as a public contract, which is why it had to carry a lexer shim
# rather than wait for a value fixture to notice.
# val is omitted where it is not meaningful (#ZZ, #BD, fixed punctuation) —
# Go spells "no value" as an empty map and TS as undefined, so rendering it
# would encode a representation difference as a token difference. Non-finite
# numbers use the corpus markers, because the JSON encoders disagree about
# EVERY ROW WAS GENERATED BY MEASURING BOTH PORTS AND DIFFING, never
# The first block is the classes that actually broke in production.
